aspects.says: The split of sampled bytes between methods is rougher than the total, so per-method figures are a ranking rather than a measurement.
basis: section:A JFR Allocation Sample Stands for All the Bytes Since the Previous One
aspects.reason: how far a per-method figure is off depends on where the sampler happens to land, which no deterministic test can pin down

aspects.says: An allocation sample's top frame is usually the JDK's allocation helper; the application method responsible is the first of its frames further down the stack.
basis: section:A JFR Allocation Sample Stands for All the Bytes Since the Previous One

aspects.says: A jdk.ObjectAllocationSample's weight is what its thread allocated since its previous sample, so summing weights estimates allocated bytes, and counting samples does not.
basis: section:A JFR Allocation Sample Stands for All the Bytes Since the Previous One

aspects.says: Thread.print reports a deadlock only for a cycle of locks; threads stuck behind a holder that waits on something else get no deadlock section.
basis: section:A Thread Dump Names a Deadlock Cycle, Not a Thread Stuck Behind a Holder That Waits

aspects.says: Without -Xmx the maximum heap is MaxRAMPercentage (25) of the memory the JVM sees, which in a container is its limit; MaxRAMPercentage changes the share and -Xmx overrides it.
basis: section:Without -Xmx the Heap Is a Quarter of the Memory the JVM Sees

aspects.says: A thread BLOCKED on a monitor names the object's address; the thread whose stack lists that address as locked is the one it waits for, and two objects of one class are two locks.
basis: section:A Thread Dump Names a Deadlock Cycle, Not a Thread Stuck Behind a Holder That Waits

aspects.says: GC.heap_info reports as used every byte in the regions handed out, garbage included; live data is what a full collection leaves, and a leak is that figure climbing from one full collection to the next.
basis: section:GC.heap_info Counts Garbage as Used; Live Data Is What a Full Collection Leaves

aspects.says: A plain jcmd GC.class_histogram (like jmap -histo:live) runs a full stop-the-world collection before counting; with -all it collects nothing and counts garbage too.
basis: section:GC.heap_info Counts Garbage as Used; Live Data Is What a Full Collection Leaves

aspects.says: jdk.JavaMonitorEnter names the monitor's class, the waiter and the previous owner, for waits of 20 ms or more by default; waits for a ReentrantLock are jdk.ThreadPark events instead.
basis: section:JFR Lock Events Name the Lock, the Waiter and the Previous Owner, Above a Threshold

aspects.says: Stacks, class metadata, compiled code, the collector's structures and direct buffers are committed outside the heap, so a container limit must hold more than -Xmx, and exceeding it is OOMKilled with no OutOfMemoryError.
basis: section:The Process Is Bigger Than the Heap

aspects.says: Small memories get a 126 MB floor or 50 % of the memory, and with one CPU the JVM picks the Serial collector instead of G1.
basis: section:Without -Xmx the Heap Is a Quarter of the Memory the JVM Sees
aspects.reason: the JVM's launch-time ergonomics, which a test cannot change for the JVM it runs in

aspects.says: A thread keeps its monitors while it parks, sleeps or reads; only Object.wait() gives up the one it waits on, though the dump still lists it as locked below a waiting-on line.
basis: section:A Thread Dump Names a Deadlock Cycle, Not a Thread Stuck Behind a Holder That Waits
